question: Find the difference between a discount of 32% on an item marked for ₹1,000 and two successive discounts of 20% and 12% on the same item.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between a single discount of (x + y)% and successive discounts of x% and y% is always given by the formula (x × y / 100)%.

Here, the first discount x = 20% and the second discount y = 12%.

Difference % = (20 × 12) / 100 = 2.4%

Difference in Amount = 2.4% of ₹1000

Difference = (2.4 / 100) × 1000 = ₹24

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹1,000

Single discount = 32%

Successive discounts = 20% and 12%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − Discount / 100)

Effective Discount % = x + y − (x × y / 100)

 
 
 

 
 

 
 MP = ₹1000

 SP = ₹680
 Discount = ₹320

 
•

 After 1st = ₹800

 
• 
 −12%
 
 SP = ₹704
 Discount = ₹296

 Diff = 320 − 296 = ₹24

**Calculations:**

**Case 1: Single Discount of 32%**

⇒ Discount Amount = 32% of 1000

⇒ Discount = (32 / 100) × 1000 = ₹320

**Case 2: Successive Discounts of 20% and 12%**

⇒ Effective Discount = 20 + 12 − (20 × 12 / 100)

⇒ Effective Discount = 32 − 2.4 = 29.6%

⇒ Discount Amount = 29.6% of 1000

⇒ Discount = (29.6 / 100) × 1000 = ₹296

**Finding the difference:**

⇒ Difference in discount amounts = ₹320 − ₹296

⇒ Difference = ₹24

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of x% and y% are applied, the final effective single discount is always given by the formula: [x + y − (x × y / 100)]%.

Flat vs Successive Discount

For a flat discount equal to (x + y)% and successive discounts of x% and y%, the successive discount value will always be smaller than the flat discount by exactly (x × y / 100)%.

Marked Price & Selling Price

Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount Amount. The discount percentage is always calculated based strictly on the Marked Price of an article.
